question: Which of the following is a key feature of the Right to Information Act? (RRB Paramedical (13/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Only MPs can ask for information
Citizens must get court approval to ask questions
Officials can hide any data
Citizens can access government records and decisions
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Citizens can access government records and decisions

Explanation:
The Right to Information Act (RTI Act) 2005 is a landmark Indian law that empowers citizens to access government records and decisions. It promotes transparency and accountability in public administration. Any citizen can legally request information from public authorities without needing court approval. Officials must provide information within 30 days or face penalties. The Act is not limited to MPs; it applies to all citizens. While most information is accessible, certain exemptions exist, such as those related to national security. The RTI Act ensures that government functioning is open to public scrutiny, thereby strengthening democracy.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the RTI Act enacted? → 2005
☛ What is the time limit to provide information? → 30 days
☛ Which information can be withheld? → Related to national security
☛ What is the purpose of RTI? → Transparency and accountability
☛ Who can seek information? → Any citizen

question: Which of the following provisions in the Indian Constitution deals with the duty of the State to separate the judiciary from the executive? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 2)
options: Article 51
Article 50
Article 44
Article 48A
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 50

Explanation:
Article 50 of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy. It deals with the separation of the judiciary from the executive in public services. This provision aims to ensure judicial independence by preventing interference from the executive branch. It is a guiding principle for policy-making, though not enforceable by courts. Article 50 is found in Part IV of the Constitution. Other options: Article 44 relates to Uniform Civil Code, Article 48A relates to environment protection, and Article 51 relates to international peace and security.

☛ Article 44 relates to? → Uniform Civil Code
☛ Article 48A relates to? → Protection of environment
☛ Article 51 relates to? → International peace and security
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्रावधान कार्यपालिका से न्यायपालिका को पृथक करने के राज्य के कर्तव्य से संबंधित है? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 2)
options_hi: अनुच्छेद 51
अनुच्छेद 50
अनुच्छेद 44
अनुच्छेद 48A
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 50

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 50 राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों में शामिल है। यह प्रावधान कार्यपालिका से न्यायपालिका को पृथक करने के राज्य के कर्तव्य से संबंधित है। इसका उद्देश्य न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करना है ताकि न्यायपालिका बिना किसी दबाव के न्याय कर सके। यह प्रावधान संविधान के भाग IV में आता है जो नीति निदेशक सिद्धांतों से संबंधित है। हालांकि यह न्यायालय द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय नहीं है, लेकिन यह सरकार के नीति-निर्माण में मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांत है। अनुच्छेद 44 समान नागरिक संहिता, अनुच्छेद 48A पर्यावरण संरक्षण, और अनुच्छेद 51 अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति से संबंधित है।

question: Which of the following objectives is stated in Article 38 of the Indian Constitution? (RRB JE (25/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: To establish military rule for national security
To establish a social order based on justice—social, economic, and political
To guarantee employment to all citizens
To provide equal education opportunities for all
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To establish a social order based on justice—social, economic, and political

Explanation:
Article 38 of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy. It directs the State to strive to establish a social order based on social, economic, and political justice. This provision aims to create a just society where all citizens have equal opportunities. It is mentioned in Part IV of the Constitution. Other options like establishing military rule, guaranteeing employment, or providing equal education opportunities are not covered under Article 38 but under other articles. This article is non-justiciable, meaning it cannot be enforced by courts but serves as a guiding principle for governance.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What does Article 38 deal with? → Social order based on social, economic, and political justice
☛ Which part of the Constitution contains Article 38? → Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy)
☛ What does 'State' mean in Article 38? → Public authorities including government and Parliament
☛ Which aspects of justice are emphasized in Article 38? → Social, economic, and political justice
☛ What type of right is Article 38? → Non-justiciable (cannot be enforced by courts)
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 38 में निम्नलिखित में से किस उद्देश्य का उल्लेख किया गया है? (RRB JE (25/02/2026) Shift 3)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 38 राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों में शामिल है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य को निर्देश देता है कि वह एक ऐसी सामाजिक व्यवस्था स्थापित करने का प्रयास करे जो सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक न्याय पर आधारित हो। इसका उद्देश्य नागरिकों के लिए न्यायपूर्ण समाज का निर्माण करना है, जहाँ सभी को समान अवसर मिलें। यह अनुच्छेद भाग IV में आता है, जो राज्य के नीति-निदेशक तत्वों से संबंधित है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के लिए सैन्य शासन, रोजगार की गारंटी या समान शिक्षा के अवसर अनुच्छेद 38 में नहीं बल्कि अन्य अनुच्छेदों में वर्णित हैं।

question: Which of the following objectives is mentioned in Article 39 of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: To organise agriculture and animal husbandry
To ensure equal justice and provide free legal aid
To promote equal pay for equal work for both men and women
To organise village panchayats
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To promote equal pay for equal work for both men and women

Explanation:
Article 39 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution. It directs the State to ensure equal standard of living and adequate means of livelihood for all citizens. Specifically, it mandates equal pay for equal work for both men and women, promoting gender equality and preventing workplace discrimination. Other options like organising agriculture, free legal aid, and village panchayats are covered in different parts of the Constitution.

question: According to the Gandhian principles incorporated in the Directive Principles of State Policy, the State shall endeavor to promote: (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Large-scale corporate farming
Industrialization in urban areas
Cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas
Foreign trade agreements
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas

Explanation:
The Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV of the Indian Constitution include Gandhian principles. Article 43 directs the State to promote cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas. This is based on Mahatma Gandhi's economic philosophy emphasizing decentralization and village self-reliance. Gandhian principles focus on self-sufficient villages, small-scale industries, and local production. Options like large-scale corporate farming or industrialization in urban areas do not align with Gandhian ideals. These principles aim to reduce inequality and promote rural development.

☛ Gandhian principles include → Village panchayats, cottage industries, prohibition

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में व्यक्तिगत या सहकारी आधार पर कुटीर उद्योग

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांतों में गांधीवादी सिद्धांत शामिल हैं। अनुच्छेद 43 के अनुसार, राज्य कुटीर उद्योगों को व्यक्तिगत या सहकारी आधार पर ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में बढ़ावा देने का प्रयास करेगा। यह गांधीजी के आर्थिक दर्शन पर आधारित है, जो विकेंद्रीकरण एवं ग्राम स्वराज्य पर जोर देता है। गांधीवादी सिद्धांतों में आत्मनिर्भर गाँवों, छोटे पैमाने के उद्योगों और स्थानीय उत्पादन की अवधारणा निहित है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे बड़े पैमाने पर कॉर्पोरेट कृषि या शहरी औद्योगीकरण गांधीवादी दृष्टिकोण के अनुरूप नहीं हैं।

question: Which Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment in 2002? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 3)
options: To provide opportunities for education to children aged 6–14 years
To promote harmony among all people of India
To safeguard public property
To uphold and protect the sovereignty of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To provide opportunities for education to children aged 6–14 years

Explanation:
The 86th Constitutional Amendment of 2002 made Right to Education a fundamental right under Article 21A and added a new fundamental duty under Article 51A(k). This duty requires parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14 years. The amendment was a significant step towards making education compulsory. Earlier, there were 10 fundamental duties added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. The 86th Amendment increased this number to 11. It emphasized the importance of education as both a right and a duty.

question: Under which Article does the Supreme Court have the power of judicial review? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Article 30
Article 72
Article 32
Article 124
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 32

Explanation:
Article 32 of the Indian Constitution grants the Supreme Court the power of judicial review. Under this article, any individual can directly approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights. It is considered the 'soul of the Constitution'. Article 32 empowers the court to issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari. This forms the basis of judicial review, allowing the court to examine the constitutionality of laws. Other options: Article 30 deals with minority educational institutions, Article 72 with the President's pardoning power, and Article 124 with the establishment of the Supreme Court.

question: The power to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights is vested in_____ . (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)

Session court and High Courts
Supreme Court and High Courts
solution:

Explanation:
Under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court has the power to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. question: Article _________ describes the procedure for joint sitting of both Houses of the Parliament in certain cases. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 3)

Article 104
Article 115
Article 108
solution:

Explanation:
Article 108 of the Indian Constitution describes the procedure for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament in certain cases. question: According to Article 243Q, the level of municipality for a transitional area will be designated as a _________. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution empowers the administrator to promulgate ordinances during recess of the Legislature in Union Territories? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: 241
239
239AA
239B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 239B

Explanation:
Article 239B of the Indian Constitution empowers the administrator of a Union Territory to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the Legislature. This article is analogous to the President's ordinance-making power under Article 123, but applies to Union Territories. An ordinance promulgated by the administrator has the same force and effect as an act passed by the Legislature. However, it ceases to operate six weeks after the reassembly of the Legislature or if disapproved by the Legislative Assembly. Article 239 deals with the administration of Union Territories, 239AA contains special provisions for Delhi, and 241 deals with High Courts.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति को विभिन्न राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में अनुसूचित जातियों को निर्दिष्ट करने का अधिकार देता है? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 3)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 341

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 341 राष्ट्रपति को अधिकार देता है कि वह किसी राज्य या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के संबंध में उन जातियों को निर्दिष्ट करे जिन्हें उस राज्य या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश के लिए अनुसूचित जाति माना जाएगा। यह प्रावधान संविधान के भाग XVI (अनुसूचित जातियों, अनुसूचित जनजातियों और पिछड़े वर्गों से संबंधित विशेष प्रावधान) के अंतर्गत आता है। राष्ट्रपति इस प्रयोजन के लिए लोक अधिसूचना द्वारा आदेश जारी करता है। इसके अलावा, संसद किसी भी अनुसूचित जाति की सूची में संशोधन या परिवर्तन कर सकती है, लेकिन केवल कानून द्वारा। अनुच्छेद 330 लोकसभा में अनुसूचित जातियों के लिए सीटों के आरक्षण से संबंधित है, अनुच्छेद 342 अनुसूचित जनजातियों के बारे में है, और अनुच्छेद 344 राजभाषा आयोग से संबंधित है।

question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates the power of the Rajya Sabha from the Lok Sabha? (RRB JE (20/02/2026) Shift 1)
options: Rajya Sabha can initiate a motion of no-confidence against the Council of Ministers
Rajya Sabha can amend Money Bills
Rajya Sabha has equal power with Lok Sabha in all financial matters
Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to make laws on State subjects
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to make laws on State subjects

Explanation:
The Rajya Sabha does not have the power to legislate on state subjects, but it can authorise Parliament to do so in the national interest under Article 249. This requires a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting. The authorisation is valid for a maximum of one year and can be extended. Other options are incorrect because the Rajya Sabha cannot initiate a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers, cannot amend Money Bills, and does not have equal power with the Lok Sabha in financial matters. The Lok Sabha has supremacy in financial legislation.

question: Which of the following cabinet committees is NOT headed by the Prime Minister? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Cabinet committee on employment and skill development
Cabinet committee on economic affairs
Cabinet committee on investment and growth
Cabinet committee on parliamentary affairs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cabinet committee on parliamentary affairs

Explanation:
In India, cabinet committees are formed to streamline government functioning. The Prime Minister chairs most key committees such as the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development, and Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth. However, the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs is chaired by the Home Minister, not the Prime Minister. This committee is responsible for advancing the government's legislative agenda in Parliament and ensuring cooperation in the house. Therefore, it is the committee that is NOT headed by the Prime Minister.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संसदीय कार्यों की मंत्रिमंडल समिति

Explanation:
भारत में मंत्रिमंडल समितियाँ सरकार के कामकाज को सुचारू बनाने के लिए बनाई जाती हैं। प्रधानमंत्री अधिकांश महत्वपूर्ण समितियों जैसे आर्थिक कार्यों की मंत्रिमंडल समिति, रोजगार और कौशल विकास की मंत्रिमंडल समिति, तथा निवेश और वृद्धि की मंत्रिमंडल समिति की अध्यक्षता करते हैं। हालाँकि, संसदीय कार्यों की मंत्रिमंडल समिति की अध्यक्षता गृह मंत्री करते हैं, न कि प्रधानमंत्री। यह समिति संसद में सरकार के विधायी एजेंडे को आगे बढ़ाने और सदन में सहयोग सुनिश्चित करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है। इसलिए, यह वह समिति है जिसकी अध्यक्षता प्रधानमंत्री नहीं करते हैं।
